APPROVED_OPERATIONAL_REQUIREMENTS: exactly ten documented ansibleops resource types and interfaces
provider source local/ansibleops version 0.1.0 and supplied local inventory
Terraform Core is sole durable state authority
stable identity from documented external object key
native Linux side-effect-free read/refresh with missing/wrong-kind absence and drift reflection
publish Terraform state only after successful mutation; failure/timeout/cancel preserves prior state and retryability
structured ansible-playbook argv with cleanup on every terminal outcome and no full command output in state
canonical normalization for modes unordered values account observations and cron defaults
Go 1.24 current Plugin Framework and Terraform CLI 1.10.5 compatibility
no null_resource terraform_data provisioners manual state edits or provider-owned durable store

APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.OBJECTIVE: Complete the ten-resource ansibleops provider as one coherent Terraform lifecycle/reconciliation system.
APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.PERSONA: Platform engineer maintaining an internal Terraform provider for local Linux configuration through Ansible.

COMPONENT_GRAPH: Terraform Plugin Framework provider registration/configuration and runtime preflight
native Linux observation layer for filesystem/content/accounts/groups/cron
ten differentiated resource implementations: file directory copy template line block symlink user group cron

STATE_MODEL.ephemeral_state: Generated Ansible playbooks and process output are runtime-only; playbooks are cleaned on every terminal outcome and full output is not durable resource state.
STATE_MODEL.external_state: Linux filesystem, passwd/group databases and per-user crontabs are authoritative external objects.
STATE_MODEL.identity: Each resource ID derives only from its documented external object key and remains stable across mutable attribute updates.
STATE_MODEL.mutation: Create/Update/Delete use Ansible and publish new Terraform state only after successful external mutation.
STATE_MODEL.observation: Read/refresh performs native observation only and maps missing/wrong-kind ownership to absence plus canonical observed values.
STATE_MODEL.terraform_state: Terraform Core is the only durable Terraform state authority; provider methods publish through Plugin Framework APIs only.

SOLVER_VISIBLE_DOC_PLAN: docs/resource-reference.md for exact ten resource schemas identities and family semantics
configuration inventory and build/smoke scripts for runtime/operator entrypoints
PRODUCTION_CHARACTERISTICS: real Terraform provider process using current Plugin Framework
stable ownership identities over persistent external Linux state
process timeout cancellation cleanup and argv safety
cross-resource canonical normalization and idempotent convergence
scoped shared backing-store ownership for line/block/cron
outputs.SCALE_FIT: large_system_strict is natural: shared provider/lifecycle/runner/observation layers plus ten distinct resource families require substantive reachable implementation well beyond a localized wrapper without padding; behavioral breadth arises from state transitions, drift, ownership, process failures and family-specific semantics.
outputs.DATA_VOLUME_PLAN: Not a record-oriented business-data task. Production realism comes from persistent Linux object state and repeated Terraform lifecycle transitions rather than a synthetic bulk dataset.
UNRESOLVED_RISKS: A3 must derive coupled incomplete-behavior topology from these clean boundaries without one-defect-per-resource padding.
A2B must preserve docs as technical contracts rather than exposing defect locations or repair recipes.
